learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Exit misses may release one bounded function-specific repair and one fresh re-entry.

items.title: Starting check: read the side chain
items.prompt: Which side chain is most hydrophobic?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: classify a carboxylate
items.prompt: At a stated pH, a side chain is present as −COO⁻. Which classification fits?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: classify a neutral polar group
items.prompt: A side chain contains an uncharged hydroxyl group. Which description is most appropriate?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: select an ionic partner
items.prompt: A positively charged side chain is exposed on a protein surface. Which partner can form a favorable ionic interaction?
options: A buried hydrocarbon with no charge
A peptide carbon atom without formal charge
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: classify and place
items.prompt: A side chain contains a protonated amine under the stated condition. Which prediction is best?
options: It is neutral and favors a dry hydrocarbon core
It is acidic, negatively charged, and repels water
It is nonpolar but forms no interactions
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: mutate a buried residue
items.prompt: A buried hydrocarbon side chain in a soluble protein core is replaced by a permanently charged side chain. What is the most direct likely effect?
options: The peptide bonds are all hydrolyzed
A buried charge destabilizes core packing
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: classify in order
items.prompt: Which side chain is acidic and hydrophilic under a condition where it is deprotonated?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify an amide
items.prompt: A side chain is a neutral amide with a carbonyl and N−H group. Which tendency is best?
options: Strongly hydrophobic with no hydrogen bonding
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: match residue to environment
items.prompt: Which replacement is most likely to disrupt a dry hydrophobic core?
options: Hydrocarbon replaced by an isolated charged group
Small nonpolar group replaced by a larger nonpolar group
Surface carboxylate replaced by surface amide
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: mutate a surface residue
items.prompt: An exposed charged residue is replaced by a nonpolar hydrocarbon side chain. Which direct tendency is most plausible?
options: The new side chain becomes more water-compatible
A hydrophobic patch may become exposed to water
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Starting check: identify a zwitterion
items.prompt: Which backbone form is dipolar and has net charge zero before side-chain charge?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: sum charges
items.prompt: An amino acid has NH₃⁺, COO⁻, and an uncharged side chain. What is its net charge?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: acidic conditions
items.prompt: For an amino acid without an ionizable side chain, strongly acidic conditions favor which net-charge direction?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: identify chirality
items.prompt: Which α carbon is achiral?
options: An α carbon bonded to four different substituents
An α carbon bonded to two hydrogen atoms
An α carbon with one hydrogen and three different nonhydrogen groups
An α carbon in a specified R configuration
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: use a charge ledger
items.prompt: A stated amino acid form has NH₃⁺, COO⁻, and a side chain carrying −1. What is the net charge?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: reduce a disulfide
items.prompt: A protein’s two regions are connected by one cystine disulfide bond. A reducing reagent acts without hydrolyzing peptide bonds. What is the direct result?
options: The S−S cross-link is broken toward two thiols
A new peptide bond forms between the regions
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: use n−1
items.prompt: How many peptide bonds join six residues in one linear chain?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: hydrolyze a tripeptide
items.prompt: Complete hydrolysis of a linear tripeptide gives which result?

Three bonds cleaved and two residues released
One bond cleaved and three residues released
No bonds cleaved and one residue released
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: distinguish oxidation and reduction
items.prompt: Which change forms a cystine disulfide from two cysteine thiols?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: break an interchain link
items.prompt: Two peptide chains are joined only by a disulfide bond. What can selective reduction do?
options: Fuse the two backbones into one longer peptide
Separate the chains by breaking the S−S link
Hydrolyze every residue from both chains
Convert all amino acids to cysteine
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.
